title: Angry at God
hook: Job and the Psalms show anger can be prayer
tomorrow: Val says she'll never forgive Nico. does she have to?

segments.voice: Yesterday, John of the Cross and the dark that comes from too much light: near in the dark. Today, the dark gets loud.
screen: `NEAR IN THE DARK.` → `THE DARK GETS LOUD.`

segments.voice: A cupboard door slammed harder than it needed to be. A text typed in all caps, then deleted. Some news lands and the anger has nowhere to go. And if you grew up praying, there's a second worry under the first one: am I even allowed to be angry at God? The Bible answers with its own prayers. Yes. You can yell at God and still be praying.
screen: `A SLAMMED CUPBOARD.` → `ALLOWED TO BE ANGRY AT GOD?` → `YELLING CAN BE PRAYING.`

segments.voice: Job loses his children, his wealth and his health, and sits down in the ashes. Then he opens his mouth, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Let the day perish wherein I was born." Later: "I will speak in the bitterness of my soul." His friends rush in with neat answers that defend God. At the end, God speaks, and tells the friends they have not spoken rightly about him, the way his servant Job has. The one who argued is the one God backs. The psalms do the same thing. "How long, O Lord, wilt thou forget me unto the end?" Complaint is written right into the prayer book, and Catholics pray those psalms in the Liturgy of the Hours. Here's one to tell a friend tonight: when Jesus cries from the cross, "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" he's praying the opening of a psalm. The anger in all these prayers is said to God, not muttered about him behind his back. It keeps talking. That's why he can take it.
screen: `JOB: LET THE DAY PERISH.` · `GOD BACKS THE ONE WHO ARGUED.` · `HOW LONG, O LORD?` · `WHY HAST THOU FORSAKEN ME?` · then, large: `HE CAN TAKE IT.`

segments.voice: Say one honest sentence out loud, quietly, the one you've been holding back: how long, or why, or this isn't fair. Don't soften it. If you pray, say it to God, the way Job did, then sit in the quiet that follows and let it be heard.
Angry at God. The anger people hide, prayed out loud by Job, by the psalms, and from the cross.
Carry this: he can take it, the way he took Job's bitterness and the psalm's how long. Good night.

screen: `DAY 1713 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: VAL SAYS SHE'LL NEVER FORGIVE NICO. DOES SHE HAVE TO?`

howItsDone: Catholics pray the psalms, laments included, in the Liturgy of the Hours and at Mass, and the Church reads the Passion, with Jesus's cry from the cross, on Palm Sunday and Good Friday.

myth: "the patience of Job" means Job never complained
Job curses the day he was born and argues with God at length.
in the end, God sides with Job's friends, who defended him
God says the friends did not speak rightly about him, as Job did.
Jesus on the cross prays the opening of a psalm
my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me: the start of Psalm 21 in the Douay, 22 in many Bibles.

fork.setup: a friend's mom just lost her job. a relative tells her, "don't be mad at God, it's disrespectful." what do the psalms suggest instead?
options: bring the anger to God in words, the way the psalms do.
swallow it and give thanks, so the anger can't grow.
stop praying until the anger passes on its own.
fork.reveal: the psalms pray how long and why, and God backs Job over his tidy friends. anger said to God is still prayer. he can take it.

original.note: Latin, Psalm 12:1 in the Vulgate: how long, O Lord? the psalm's complaint in the Church's old Latin.

trapdoor: what you thought: being angry at God is the opposite of faith.
what it means: Job, the psalms and Jesus on the cross bring anger to God as prayer; he can take it.
what a scholar hears: the lament psalms; Job 42:7's verdict for Job over his friends; Jesus praying the opening of Psalm 22 (21 in the Douay) in Matthew 27:46.
guess: bringing your rage to God, as prayer
losing your faith after something awful
blaming God so you don't have to grieve

chat.says: Doña Carmen's going into hospice. Abuela slammed the cabinet and said she's mad at God. is that a sin??
options: Not the way Job did it. He told God straight, and God said Job spoke rightly.
Probably. Real faith means accepting it quietly, so she should calm down first.
It's fine as long as she keeps it to herself and never says it to God.
chat.meaning: Job cursed his birthday and argued, and God said he spoke rightly. The psalms and Jesus on the cross pray anger too. He can take it.

Job.meaning: a man in the Bible who loses everything and argues with God

psalms.meaning: the Bible's book of song-prayers, prayed by Jews and Christians

Liturgy of the Hours.meaning: the Church's daily round of prayer, built from the psalms

Douay-Rheims.meaning: an old English Catholic translation of the Bible
